battle.name: 壽春之戰
battle.theater: 淮南西路壽春府淮河南岸
battle.brief: 淳祐四年（1244）冬，蒙古軍進攻淮南西路壽春府，南宋遣趙葵、孟珙分率兩淮與荊襄之兵北援，於壽春城下展開攻營與反攻之戰，宋軍奪壘破敵、追奔數十里，斬獲以萬計，淮南門戶為之一安。卡面希臘火屬拜占庭七世紀的噴射燃燒劑，此役未見其用，僅能對照蒙古攻城所用的火藥火油。

kit.name: 希臘火
kit.history: 配在銅管裡的燃燒劑。配方是帝國的機密，配方和船一起沉了。

countries: 淳祐四年（1244）冬季，戰場在今安徽省淮南市壽縣一帶，壽春府城踞淮河中游南岸，淝水於城東入淮，水陸兩路皆可通軍。交戰的一方是蒙古帝國：自1235年起分路南征的蒙古遠征軍，攻下襄陽、樊城、鄂州之後，把河南與荊襄變成南下的跳板，1240年代前期在兩淮與河南用兵的是大汗廷直接調度的蒙古宿將，兵員以蒙古本部騎兵為骨幹，配以金朝降軍改編而成的漢軍步兵、攻城器械與工匠隊，糧秣多就地取之於汴、蔡、宿一線的屯田與徵發。另一方是南宋：淮南西路、淮東兩路的地方軍兵與孟珙所部荊湖北路邊軍為主體，趙葵以兩淮制置的名分統率淮東、淮西兵，孟珙以荊湖北路安撫使兼知襄陽府節制襄、鄂舟師與步騎，朝廷則由中書、樞密院調度錢糧與援軍。壽春是淮南門戶，向西可援蔡州，向北可窺宋、汴，向南則通廬州，是蒙古南下最想拔掉的一枚釘子。
countriesEn: The campaign of the winter of the fourth year of the Chunxi era (1244) was fought around present-day Shouxian in Huainan, Anhui, where the prefectural seat of Shouchun stood on the south bank of the middle Huai River, the Fei River joining the Huai just east of the walls, so that troops could move by water and by land. One belligerent was the Mongol Empire. The expeditions that had marched south in several columns since 1235 had taken Xiangyang, Fancheng and Ezhou, turning Henan and Jingxiang into the springboard for further advance; the operations in the Two Huai and in Henan during the early 1240s were directed by Mongol veterans dispatched directly from the Great Khan's court, with the Mongol cavalry as the backbone of the force, supported by Han Chinese infantry recruited from surrendered Jin troops, siege machines and artisan corps, and drawing grain and supplies largely from the strip of Henan around Bianjing, Caizhou and Suzhou. The other belligerent was the Southern Song, whose army was made up chiefly of the levies of Huainan West and Huainan East circuits together with Meng Gong's frontier forces in Jinghu North. Zhao Kui commanded the troops of the Two Huai in his capacity as circuit commissioner, while Meng Gong, pacification commissioner of Jinghu North and governor of Xiangyang, controlled the river flotilla and the infantry and cavalry of Xiang and E. The court in Lin'an, for its part, moved money, grain and reinforcements through the Secretariat and the Bureau of Military Affairs. Shouchun was the gate of Huainan: from it one could relieve Caizhou to the west, look down on Song and Bian to the north, and reach Luzhou to the south. It was exactly the nail in the board that the Mongols most wanted to pull.
people: 留下姓名的，多半在宋方。孟珙是此役最關鍵的策劃者：他出身江陵孟氏，紹興末年已領兵，嘉熙、淳祐年間坐鎮荊襄，把襄陽經營成南朝北出的支點；他主張據襄以窺蔡，即先鞏固襄、鄂，再向北控制蔡州、壽春，切斷蒙古在河南的南北通道，淳祐四年他親率荊襄兵北上，與趙葵會師。趙葵是掛帥的主將，趙氏宗室出身，與兄趙范先後出領兩淮軍務；趙范在淳祐四年病卒軍中，兩淮兵權一度盡歸趙葵，此役也成為他一生最重的功業之一。呂文德等沿江、兩淮宿將參與其事，具體分工事各書記載不一。蔡州守軍在蒙古圍困下屢次告急，其守將姓名與城防細節，現存宋元史籍多付闕如。蒙古方面的主將姓名，宋人記載幾乎全缺，只能確定指揮體系由大汗廷在河南的經略機構調度，漢軍宿將所部為攻城骨幹。值得一記的是孟珙本人：十年前他曾護送金哀宗遺骨自蔡州返臨安，十年後又率兵打到蔡州城下，一座城的兩次意義在他身上交接。
peopleEn: The names that survive are mostly on the Song side. Meng Gong was the chief planner of the campaign. He came from the Meng clan of Jiangling, had already led troops by the end of the Shaoxing reign, and in the Jiaxi and Chunxi years sat in Jingxiang, turning Xiangyang into a hinge for a northern thrust by the southern court. His plan was to hold Xiangyang in order to look toward Caizhou: secure Xiang and E first, then press north to control Caizhou and Shouchun and sever the north-south corridor that the Mongols held in Henan. In the fourth year of Chunxi he led the Jingxiang troops north in person and joined forces with Zhao Kui. Zhao Kui was the field commander, a member of the imperial Zhao clan, and he and his elder brother Zhao Fan had in turn taken charge of the armies of the Two Huai. Zhao Fan died of illness in the field during the fourth year of Chunxi, and the command of the Two Huai forces fell for a time to Zhao Kui alone; this campaign became the heaviest of Zhao Kui's career. Generals such as Lü Wende, veterans of the river front and the Two Huai, also took part, though the surviving books disagree about the division of their tasks. The garrison of Caizhou, besieged and repeatedly appealing for help, is not named in the Song and Yuan histories that remain, and no detail of its defences survives. The names of the Mongol commanders are almost entirely absent from the Song accounts; all that can be established is that the command structure ran through the Mongol administrative office for Henan, with Han Chinese generals and their men forming the siege corps. One detail is worth recording about Meng Gong himself: ten years earlier he had escorted the remains of the last Jin emperor out of Caizhou back to Lin'an, and ten years later he led an army to the very walls of that same city, so that the two meanings of one place were handed across in his own person.
kits: 卡面的希臘火，是拜占庭帝國七世紀的噴射式燃燒劑：銅管加虹吸管把以石油為基底的燃燒劑點燃噴出，覆蓋敵船甲板或城牆根部。它的真正歷史只有一段：配方屬帝國最高機密，配方隨一次海難沉沒，之後只剩零星描述流傳——拉丁文獻 De igne Graeco 留下的硫磺、生石灰與石油之比，九至十三世紀阿拉伯與蒙古史料裡反覆出現的「火油」投擲，一一都是這條技術譜系的餘波。要緊的是，關於希臘火在壽春之戰中的實際運用，《宋史》《元史》一字未提，連攻城焚燒器的記載也只到火藥陶罐與火油。真正在壽春城下的，是同時代兩套更樸素的燃燒兵器：蒙古攻城序列裡配重投石機所擲的陶罐火藥、以火油引燃的燃燒瓶，以及撞車、雲梯、穴地與覆土的攻城塔；宋軍的火力骨幹則是蹶張硬弩（神臂弓）、步弩與砲石，另有火藥火箭與霹靂火藥一類的爆炸性投射物。戰馬方面，蒙古本部騎兵自帶備馬，漢軍步卒靠步盾與標槍、弓箭抵禦；糧秣靠牛車與騾車，而壽春之戰的補給線則繫在淮河與淝水的水陸轉運上。
kitsEn: The Greek fire shown on the card is the seventh-century Byzantine projected burning mixture: a copper tube and siphon arrangement that lit a petroleum-based incendiary and sprayed it over an enemy deck or the foot of a wall. Its true history occupies a single span. The formula was the empire's highest secret, and the formula went down with a ship in a maritime disaster; afterwards only scattered descriptions survived, among them the Latin treatise De igne Graeco with its proportions of sulphur, quicklime and petroleum, and the repeated mention of poured fire oil in the Arabic and Mongol sources of the ninth to the thirteenth centuries, all of them the afterglow of one technical lineage. What matters is that neither the Song History nor the Yuan History records a single instance of Greek fire being used at the battle of Shouchun; even the siege incendiaries are mentioned only as jars of gunpowder and as fire oil. What was actually beneath the walls of Shouchun were two humbler burning systems of the same age. In the Mongol siege sequence there were the jars of gunpowder slung by counterweight stone-throwers, fire bottles lit with oil, and battering rams, ladders, mine shafts and earth-covered siege towers. The backbone of the Song firepower was the strong crossbow drawn by several men at once, known as the divine arm bow, together with ordinary crossbows and stone shot, plus gunpowder rockets and explosive projectiles of the thunder-crash type. On the horse side, the Mongol cavalry carried its own remounts, while Han infantry relied on shields, spears and bows; grain and provisions travelled in ox and mule carts, and the supply line of the Shouchun campaign hung on the water and land transfers along the Huai and the Fei.
tactics: 壽春之戰的形狀，是一次典型的冬季攻城與反攻城。蒙古軍先抵淮南西路界上，攻壽春、掠兩淮，斷宋軍糧道；其營壘環城而列，留一面通出入，攻城用配重投石機與火藥器具，兵卒掘地道、填壕溝，企圖在冬春之間耗盡守軍的糧水。南宋的處置，是把這場救援當作一次主動的攻勢：趙葵率兩淮之兵自盱眙、泗州一線北上，孟珙率荊襄兵自鄂州溯漢水北行，兩軍在蔡州對岸與壽春之間會合；糧秣則由江、漢水路轉輸，再以車騎走陸路北上。會合之後，宋軍不急於硬攻城垣，而先打蒙古軍的野戰營壘——這是取勝的關鍵：壽春一帶多黏土，經冬雨之後道路泥濘，騎兵衝鋒受阻，漢軍步卒的長槍陣與弩手在營壘與壕溝之間發揮作用，宋軍奪壘破敵，乘勝追奔，迫蒙古軍退保。蒙古軍的游騎則不斷深入宋軍側後，割斷糧道與援軍通道，使宋軍不敢深入河南；宋軍終因糧運遲滯、援兵不繼而退回原防，這也說明宋軍雖勝一陣，卻沒有條件把勝利變成戰略成果。
tacticsEn: The shape of the battle of Shouchun was that of a typical winter siege and counter-siege. The Mongol army first reached the boundary of Huainan West circuit, attacked Shouchun and raided the Two Huai, cutting the Song supply lines. Their camps ringed the city while one side was left open for entry and exit; for the assault they used counterweight throwers and gunpowder apparatus, and the troops dug galleries and filled the ditches, hoping to exhaust the garrison's grain and water between winter and spring. The Song response was to treat the relief as an offensive in its own right. Zhao Kui took the troops of the Two Huai north from the Xuyi and Sizhou line, while Meng Gong led the Jingxiang force north from Ezhou up the Han River; the two armies met between Caizhou and Shouchun. Provisions were transferred by water along the Yangzi and the Han, then carried north by cart and horse. After the junction the Song did not hurry to batter the walls. They struck the Mongols' field encampments first, and that was the key to the victory: the ground around Shouchun was heavy clay and mud after the winter rains, so that cavalry charges lost their effect, and the Han infantry's long-spear formations and crossbowmen did the work among the camp lines and ditches. The Song took the camps, broke the enemy and pursued, forcing the Mongols to fall back behind their works. Mongol light cavalry meanwhile pushed deep into the Song flanks and rear, cutting grain routes and blocking reinforcements, so that the Song army dared not press on into Henan. In the end the Song withdrew to its original positions because the food convoys were slow and reinforcements insufficient, which shows that although the Song won an engagement, it had no means of turning that win into a strategic result.
data: 可以核的數字不多，但有幾項相當硬。時間：淳祐四年（1244）冬，蒙古軍入淮南在十一月至十二月之間，宋軍北援與壽春之戰亦在同季。地名與距離：壽春在今安徽壽縣，與蔡州（今河南汝南）直線相距約二百餘公里，近五百里；宋軍主力自鄂州起程，順漢水北行再轉陸路，全程逾千里。兵力：宋軍為兩淮地方軍兵與荊襄邊軍抽調而成的混成兵團，總數當以數萬計，各書所記互有出入，把沿途徵發的民兵一併計入者數字更大；蒙古軍以本部騎兵為骨幹，攻城漢軍另編一軍。戰果：《宋史》一系記載宋軍斬首、俘虜、馬匹、牛隻皆以萬計，然各家數目互有出入，難以逐一核對，故此處不另作推算，只取其量級。糧秣方面，宋軍糧運自襄、鄂千里轉輸，蒙古軍則就糧於汴、蔡一線的河南平原，這一條差距決定了雙方能撐多久。城池：壽春府城依淮河而築，兼有水陸兩路，蒙古圍城之日水運被切，城內存糧究竟能撐多久，各書無明確記載。
dataEn: The verifiable numbers are few, but several are hard enough. Timing: the Mongol entry into Huainan fell between the eleventh and twelfth months of the fourth year of Chunxi (1244), and the Song relief and the battle of Shouchun belong to the same season. Place and distance: Shouchun is present-day Shouxian in Anhui, roughly two hundred and some kilometres in a straight line from Caizhou, present-day Runan in Henan, close to five hundred li; the main body of the Song army set out from Ezhou, went north up the Han River and then turned overland, a route of more than a thousand li in all. Numbers of men: the Song force was a mixed corps drawn from the levies of the Two Huai and the frontier troops of Jingxiang, and its total must have counted in the tens of thousands; the books differ, and the figures grow larger when locally conscripted militia are swept into the count. On the Mongol side the backbone was the native cavalry, with the Han siege troops mustered separately. Results: the Song histories record heads taken, prisoners, horses and cattle all in the tens of thousands, though the figures differ from book to book and cannot be checked item by item, so no further calculation is attempted here and only the order of magnitude is taken. As for supply, the Song drew its grain over a thousand li from Xiangyang and Ezhou, while the Mongols foraged on the Henan plain around Bianjing and Caizhou; that single difference decided how long each side could hold. Regarding the city: the prefectural walls of Shouchun were built along the Huai River and offered both water and land routes, and once the Mongols invested the town the waterborne traffic was cut; how long the stores inside could last is not recorded.
cause: 打起來的緣由有三層。最外一層是眼前的：淳祐四年秋，蒙古軍打通河南後自北南下，進攻壽春、進圍蔡州，淮南西路告急，南宋朝廷不得不議出兵。往裡一層是蒙古的算盤：宋金以滅金之役共享河南，1234年金朝覆亡之後，河南成了蒙古的內地，蒙古得以據汴、洛、蔡，居高臨下俯瞰荊襄與兩淮；只要把壽春、蔡州一線的釘子拔掉，蒙古就能把河南與江南之間的通道握在一手，同時切斷南宋從襄、鄂向北輸血的血管。更深的一層是南宋自己的分歧：端平入洛的北伐兩度失利之後，朝廷對在北方用兵心懷疑懼，執政者擔心糧源不繼、騎兵不足；孟珙、趙葵這一批邊帥則認為一味退守只會讓蒙古逐段蠶食淮南，必須趁蒙古兵力分散、立足未穩之時，以淮西兵力的局部攻勢去爭取河南的縱深。於是這場戰爭的本質，是蒙古要拆南朝的牆，南朝要在牆上開一扇向北的窗。
causeEn: There were three layers of reason for the fighting. The outermost was immediate: in the autumn of the fourth year of Chunxi, the Mongols, having broken through Henan, came south from the north, attacked Shouchun and closed around Caizhou; Huainan West circuit was in distress and the Song court had no choice but to debate sending troops. The second layer was the Mongol calculation. The Song and the Jin had shared Henan in the war that destroyed the Jin, and after the Jin fell in 1234 Henan became Mongol interior ground, allowing the Mongols to hold Bian, Luo and Cai and look down upon Jingxiang and the Two Huai. Pull the nails of the Shouchun and Caizhou line and the Mongols would hold the corridor between Henan and the Yangzi in one hand, while cutting the artery by which the Southern Song sent blood northward from Xiang and E. The deepest layer was the division within the Southern Song itself. After the failures of the Duanping northern expeditions the court was wary of fighting in the north, and ministers feared an unreplenishable grain supply and a shortage of cavalry. Meng Gong, Zhao Kui and the other frontier commanders held the opposite view: that a purely defensive posture would hand the Mongols the Two Huai by degrees, and that while the Mongol force was still dispersed and unsettled on plain ground, a limited offensive from Huainan could be used to buy depth in Henan. The essence of the war, then, was that the Mongols meant to take down the wall of the southern court while the southern court meant to open a window in that wall facing north.
impact: 壽春之戰的直接效果是局部的：蒙古第一次大舉伸入淮南腹地的攻勢被擋回，壽春與蔡州一線在一段時間裡穩了下來，兩淮防線得以重整；而孟珙據襄以圖蔡的思路也在此役之後固定下來，成為南宋後期對蒙古作戰的基本樣式：不在河南與騎兵爭地盤，而在荊襄前沿立一個向北的支點，用局部攻勢拖住蒙古的推進速度，讓它在河南平原上背著糧草包袱。戰術層面的影響更實在：這是一場火藥兵器大規模投入淮北攻守的戰役之一，蒙古的配重投石機所擲火藥陶罐、攻城塔與穴地，宋軍的火箭、霹靂火藥與震天雷一類的爆炸器具，在壽春城下同時出現；二十餘年後襄樊之役，蒙古在攻城之中把火藥兵器用到了極致，壽春的實戰經驗可以說是那條路線的早期版本。而卡面那件希臘火，則提醒另一件事：最富戲劇性的燃燒兵器往往最先失傳，留到最後並決定勝負的，反而是配方簡單、可以大量生產的東西。
impactEn: The direct effect of Shouchun was local. The first large Mongol thrust into the belly of Huainan was thrown back, the Shouchun and Caizhou line held steady for a time, the Two Huai defences could be reorganised, and Meng Gong's idea of basing operations on Xiangyang in order to reach Caizhou was fixed after this campaign as the basic pattern of Southern Song warfare against the Mongols: not to contest Henan and its cavalry for territory, but to plant a hinge pointing north in the Jingxiang front, using limited offensives to slow the Mongol advance and keep them carrying their baggage across the Henan plain. The tactical implications were even more concrete. This was one of the campaigns in which gunpowder weapons were committed on a large scale to the fighting north of the Huai: the jars of gunpowder slung by Mongol counterweight throwers, siege towers and mine shafts on one side, and Song rockets, thunder-crash powder and shock devices of the thunder-bolt type on the other, all appearing at once beneath Shouchun. Some twenty years later, at Xiangfan, the Mongols carried gunpowder weapons to their extreme in siege work, and the practical experience of Shouchun was an early version of that road. The card's Greek fire points to a second lesson: the most dramatic burning weapon is often the first to be lost, while the thing that decides the issue at the end is the simple formula that can be produced in quantity.
result: 結果是一場沒有贏家的局部勝利。宋軍在壽春城下奪壘破敵、追奔數十里，斬獲以萬計，蒙古對淮西的攻勢被迫中止，壽春暫時保住，蔡州方向的圍困也為之鬆動；但宋軍沒有條件追擊——糧自襄、鄂千里而來，援兵不繼，游騎又橫在側後，攻勢只能停在壽春一線，蒙古在河南的根據地分毫未損。壽春之後，兩淮的防禦體系徹底定型為守勢：築城、浚壕、屯兵，倚賴襄漢與蜀口互相策應，蒙古則不急於求成，改以穩步推進的方式，逐一拔除南宋在江淮與襄漢的據點。從大歷史看，壽春之戰是南宋在1270年代全面崩潰前最後一次像樣的戰術勝利：它贏了戰場，輸了戰略，也換來二十餘年從容布置防線的時間——若那些時間用得更好，結局也許不同。
resultEn: The result was a local victory with no winner in the wider sense. The Song army took the Mongol camp at Shouchun, broke the enemy and pursued for several tens of li, taking and capturing on a scale of tens of thousands, and the Mongol offensive into Huainan was halted while Shouchun was held for a time and the siege of Caizhou eased. But the Song could not follow up: grain came over a thousand li from Xiangyang and Ezhou, reinforcements did not arrive, and Mongol light cavalry hung on the flanks and rear, so the advance had to stop on the Shouchun line, and the Mongol base in Henan was not touched at all. After Shouchun, the defensive system of the Two Huai settled definitively into a posture of defence: walls raised, ditches dredged, troops garrisoned, the fronts of Xiang-Han and of Sichuan watching each other, while the Mongols, in no hurry, changed to a steady advance and removed the Southern Song's strongpoints in the Huai-Jiang and the Xiang-Han one after another. In the larger history, the battle of Shouchun was the last respectable tactical victory the Southern Song won before its general collapse in the 1270s. It won the field and lost the strategy, and it bought more than twenty years in which the defences could be laid out at leisure; had that time been used better, the ending might have been different.
